app/(studio)/projects/runs/_runs/model.ts:18 Runs works in wall-clock job time. The technique says not to extend the product's runtime clock into wall-clock scheduling.
app/(studio)/projects/runs/_runs/model.ts:9 A read-only console: it persists no media artifacts, so there is nothing to classify.

pairs.subject: production-pipeline-phasing
pairs.evidence: packages/ui/src/components/style/LockGate.tsx:4 A style graduates candidate → proven → locked one way only: proven by operator keeps, locked by an explicit act the server admits only when the trial-coverage gate holds, and stale approvals stop vouching. The shared style asset graduates by human act against a checked gate.

techniques.evidence: packages/ui/src/components/style/LockGate.tsx:4 A one-way ratchet. The blocker is the server's own sentence, not a view's re-derivation, so the drawn gate is the gate the write enforces.

packages/ui/src/components/style/ProofSheet.tsx:6 An annotated trial crosses into asset (as the technique requires). Proofs under an earlier block are marked stale and no longer sent as references, so the style is versioned and supersession is explicit.

packages/ui/src/components/style/style.ts:11 A stale approval reads idle, not done. Trial columns count stale proofs apart and never show them as the face. Unpriced spend is counted, never zeroed (style.ts:58).

packages/ui/src/components/style/LockGate.tsx:44 Before the shared style contract can lock, it must cover a fixed battery of downstream trial problems (TrialMatrix.tsx:9). That battery is the forward list, but it is generic, not the beats of a specific project.

pairs.registryProposal: approval-reads-forward assumes the shared asset belongs to one production with a known beat list. A library-level style contract reused across projects has no beats at lock time; the technique should say whether a fixed battery of downstream trial problems satisfies the forward read, or whether the forward check must be repeated per project when the locked style is adopted.
